thread:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: kvcache-service v2.17.0 -> prod (canary 10% -> 100%). (id: dpl-20260314-089)

alice: Rolling this now, small eviction tweak + kv prefetch optimization. No expected schema changes.

carla: saw a small uptick in 5xx during canary (just monitoring), nothing alarming at 10% yet.

bob: alert: p95 latency for /generate jumped from 180ms -> 420ms in the last 3m. p99 from 620ms -> 2.1s. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.local/kvcache-service/overview

alice: @bob can you paste the p99 distribution and error breakdown?

bob: copying snippets:
```
p95: 420ms
p99: 2.1s
5xx rate: 0.12% -> 1.8%
timeouts (gateway): +9.3% failures
median token latency unaffected
```
Error codes: 502 gateway, 504 upstream-timeout, 500 internal-kv-miss

frank: I see same in logs — backend pod oom/kvcache eviction churn: lots of KV cache misses that cause full model cold starts. Example trace:
```
[2026-03-14T09:02:34Z] ERR model-infer: kvcache-miss burst=173 upstream-latency=1800ms reason="evict-after-prefetch"
[2026-03-14T09:02:36Z] WARN allocator: retry-alloc gpu0 mem-available=128MB
```

helen: Can we throttle canary to 0 and rollback? Impact on customers small so far, but SLA risk.

alice: I'm paging oncall and incident-bot. @oncall-bot assign to alice (oncall rotation).

oncall-bot: @alice is currently oncall (primary) — incident created: INC-20260314-089 (severity: high). Paging now. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Auto-detected: latency-regression + elevated-5xx for kvcache-service. Creating incident channel #incident-INC-20260314-089.

alice: I'm on it. First action: cut canary to 0 and disable kv prefetch. Can someone run rollout-cancel on dpl-20260314-089?

carla: running rollback now (kubectl rollout undo kvcache-service --to-revision=stable)
```
$ kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/kvcache-service
deployment.apps/kvcache-service rolled back to revision stable
```

carla: canary set to 0, traffic rebalanced. Watching metrics.

bob: updating: p95 -> 200ms within 90s, p99 -> 340ms, 5xx dropping to baseline. Gateway timeouts down.

frank: confirmed backend oom events stop after rollback. Looks like the eviction change caused asynchronous prefetch spikes that temporarily doubled memory working set and triggered kernel thrash on some GPU instances.

alice: Good rollback. Marking incident mitigated. Next: public/customer impact assessment and postmortem ownership.

helen: Customer impact estimate (initial): ~7-11% of live requests saw >1s latency or timeout during 09:01-09:07 UTC. No data loss. A/B customers using dedicated capacity saw lower impact.

alice: Who wants postmortem? I'll start the timeline and hand off root cause analysis to research/eng-ml for kv cache logic. Assigning action items:
- @carla: collect deploy logs, canary traffic config, rollout steps (due EOD)
- @frank: collect memory/GPU metrics + kernel logs from affected hosts (due EOD)
- @bob: export dashboard snapshots + alert history (due EOD)
- @helen: draft customer notification/incident summary (draft by 12:30 UTC)

carla: noted. attaching the deploy diff for quick look:
```
- kv_prefetch: enabled
- eviction_policy: LRU -> LRU_PLUS_TIMEOUT
- prefetch_batch: 64 -> 128
```

frank: that prefetch_batch bump is suspicious — doubling async prefetch can spike concurrent memory usage during overlap windows.

alice: Agreed. For next steps, do not re-deploy v2.17.0 until root cause confirmed. We'll create a canary with prefetch_batch=64 and a small synthetic load test.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260314-089 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem owner: alice. Ticket: PM-20260314-kvcache.

bob: Quick note: alert thresholds looked tight for p99; consider smoothing or adding a short cooldown to prevent noisy paging on transient canary behavior.

alice: Good point. Add to postmortem. Also schedule a follow-up triage with eng-ml and infra tomorrow 1400 UTC. I'll post a link in #incident-INC-20260314-089.

helen: Customer notification draft: "We briefly observed elevated timeouts and increased latency affecting a subset of requests between 09:01-09:07 UTC due to a canary deployment. Services have been rolled back and are stable. We're investigating and will follow up with a detailed postmortem."

alice: Posting that now to SEV channel and marking for legal review.

carla: adding logs bundle to ticket: s3://redwood-incident-archives/INC-20260314-089/logs.tar.gz

frank: leaving a note: infrastructure will add a safety limiter on prefetch concurrency to prevent >96 concurrent prefetch ops per GPU.

alice: Thanks all. Handoff to postmortem team. Closing thread here but keep #incident-INC-20260314-089 open for analysis. :white_check_mark:
